text: The nine fact tables are the read model in rwb_reporting (P9), built from the business events on Kafka; there is no data lake and no Power BI connection (INT-19 and INT-20 stay removed) and the dashboards and reports are served through GET /dashboards/{id} and GET /reports/{id} behind gateway-bff.
why: Arch v5 removes the lake and gives rwb-reporting its own schema, and ADR-018 and DP-17 state the read model from events as the replacement; the source document cannot keep a lake that the architecture has removed.

confirm: Data architecture team confirms the read model replaces the lake for the steering dashboard and the regulatory extract.
impact: Every fact table lands in rwb_reporting; no lake copy, no Power BI grant and no INT-19 or INT-20 interface is built.

text: Every ACE-fed fact and dimension takes its rows from the rwb-source-data contract and its snapshot(page) activity; the read model holds no recovery.v_ace_* grant and P9 never reads the ACE views directly.
why: Arch v5 keeps the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views with rwb-source-data alone and DP-05 makes the ACE read a contract call, so a reporting layer that reads the views itself contradicts both.

impact: P9 holds one contract dependency on P1 and no ACE view grant; ACE data stays inside rwb_source_data.

text: The Workbench-side facts are event-fed projections and the measures publish at 01:30 as JOB-15, triggered by Airflow with a rerun for any business date; the monthly bucket flow fact is rebuilt from the P1 snapshot(page) result for the month.
why: The job map gives the reporting extract to rwb-reporting at 01:30 and the model reads its own projections, so a nightly load from the Workbench schema and a bare monthly refresh no longer exist.

impact: Nine refresh cells change; the hold and release of a business date is a measure_publish row, not a job flag.

text: The whole read model sits in the P9 own schema rwb_reporting, and every input is named with its owning service and table from the Ownership Map: P1 for the ACE rows, P3 for case, queue and assignment, P7 for the decision ledger and the rule registry, P8 for proceeds, S2 for treatment, S4 for legal action, S5 for asset sale, S6 for lots, S7 for write-off and S9 for partner instructions.
why: Arch v5 gives each service one schema and the Ownership Map is the run fixed owner of every table, so the model cannot stay ownerless.

impact: Three columns are appended on Facts, two on Dimensions and two on Measures; no source cell changes because of this row.

text: measure_definition, measure_snapshot and measure_publish are the read-model control tables under P9 in rwb_reporting and hold the definition version, the frozen value per business date and the publish or hold decision; the queue measures stay with P3 rwb_case and are not duplicated in rwb_reporting.
why: The Ownership Map puts the three measure tables with P9 and queue_measure with P3, and the LDM gives the publish gate and the frozen flag, so the model needs them named and must not copy the P3 queue measures.

text: Each fact row carries the business date it belongs to; events are deduped in the inbox by event id and applied in business-date order, a day is reopened only while its measure_publish row is not Published and measure_snapshot.frozen is false, and any fact is rebuilt by refolding the retained topic history.
why: The target has no lake copy to fall back on, so the late-arrival and replay rule has to sit with the read model, and the LDM already provides the business date, the frozen flag and the publish status.

confirm: TechX confirms the Kafka retention window that makes a refold possible for each topic.
impact: A late event changes a day that is not yet published; a published day is frozen and corrected only by a new business date.

text: The read model keys the owner, the team and the queue by ID from the events and resolves a display name from the P3 queue_member and assignment rows behind the rwb-access masking policy; no personal data travels on an event and no name is stored in a fact table.
why: Arch v5 states that events carry IDs and facts and never personal data, while dim_org holds an owner, so the name must be resolved at read time from an owning service rather than projected from an event.

impact: Facts hold an owner ID; the name comes from P3 under the P4 masking policy and is never written to a topic.

text: The Power BI wording in LDM v8 and FSD P3 is read as consumed through rwb-reporting: the case list and the queue measures reach a dashboard through rwb-reporting's GET /dashboards/{id} and GET /reports/{id}, and no direct Power BI connection is rebuilt.
why: Arch v5 removes INT-19 and INT-20 and replaces the Power BI feed with reports from rwb-reporting, so the two documents that still say published to Power BI name a consumer that no longer exists, and this model states what replaces it.
